title: Derive the track colors
prompt:
The Design track's base color is `--track: oklch(62% 0.19 350)`, but its badge tint and active border are hand-picked hex codes. Replace them with rules that work for **any** track:

1. Badge background: mix **15%** of `--track` with **white**, in **oklch**.
2. Active card (`.is-active`) border: the track color with lightness **0.15 lower**, same chroma and hue, using relative color syntax.
3. Add a `.track-perf` class whose `--track` has the same lightness and chroma as Design, with hue **220**.

The checks read the computed OKLCH values, and also activate the Performance card to make sure your rules aren't specific to one track.
hints: `color-mix(in oklch, A 15%, B)` gives 15% of A and 85% of B.
Relative syntax starts with `from`: `oklch(from var(--track) … c h)`. The `l` channel is a number from 0 to 1.

`.badge { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--track) 15%, white); }`, `.is-active { border-inline-start-color: oklch(from var(--track) calc(l - 0.15) c h); }`, `.track-perf { --track: oklch(62% 0.19 220); }`.
explanation: Both state colors now read `--track` at the element where they're used, so every track gets its own tint and active border from one base value. `color-mix(in oklch, var(--track) 15%, white)` interpolates lightness and chroma towards white while keeping the hue, giving a pale tint (L ≈ 0.94). The relative color form unpacks `--track` into `l`, `c` and `h`, subtracts 0.15 from the lightness and repacks it, so the active border is the same pink, only darker. Because the Performance track shares L and C with Design, its colors carry the same visual weight.

checks.badge-tint: The Design badge is a 15% tint of the track color
checks.active-darker: The active border is 0.15 darker than the track
checks.perf-track: The Performance track has the same L and C with hue 220
checks.perf-badge-follows: The Performance badge tint follows its own track
checks.derived-for-new-tracks: An active Performance card gets its own darker border
